hints: At a constant speed on a level road, acceleration is zero, so the driving force equals the resistance: $F_D = 350\text{ N}$.
Use $P = F_D v$ with $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and convert the result into kW.
walkthrough:
Since the car travels at constant speed on a horizontal road, the driving force balances the resistance force:
$$F_D = 350\text{ N}$$

Calculate the power in watts and convert to kilowatts:
$$P = F_D v = 350 \times 20 = 7000\text{ W} = 7\text{ kW}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Identify the condition for motion at constant speed along a horizontal road: zero acceleration means the forward driving force $F_D$ must balance the opposing resistance $R$:
$$F_D = R = 350\text{ N}$$

State the power equation relating driving force and velocity:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Substitute $F_D = 350\text{ N}$ and constant velocity $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 350 \times 20 = 7000\text{ W}$$

Convert watts to kilowatts by dividing by $1000$:
$$P = \frac{7000}{1000} = 7\text{ kW}$$

hints: Find the driving force from the given power of $15\text{ kW} = 15000\text{ W}$ at speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $F_D = \frac{P}{v}$.
Apply Newton's second law horizontally: $F_D - 350 = 1400a$ and solve for $a$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the driving force when power is $15\text{ kW} = 15000\text{ W}$ at speed $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{15000}{20} = 750\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law horizontally with mass $m = 1400\text{ kg}$ and resistance $350\text{ N}$:
$$F_D - R = ma$$
$$750 - 350 = 1400a$$
$$400 = 1400a$$

Solve for acceleration $a$:
$$a = \frac{400}{1400} = \frac{2}{7}\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 0.286\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the relationship between power, driving force, and speed:
$$P = F_D \times v \implies F_D = \frac{P}{v}$$

Substitute power $P = 15\text{ kW} = 15000\text{ W}$ and speed $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{15000}{20} = 750\text{ N}$$

State Newton's second law in the forward horizontal direction:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
$$F_D - R = ma$$
Substitute $F_D = 750\text{ N}$, resistance $R = 350\text{ N}$, and car mass $m = 1400\text{ kg}$:
$$750 - 350 = 1400a$$
$$400 = 1400a$$

Divide both sides by $1400$ and reduce the fraction:
$$a = \frac{400}{1400} = \frac{4}{14} = \frac{2}{7}\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 0.286\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
